evidence.quote: if the data comes in as I expect I will support a similar-sized move at our July meeting.
The Fed is "all in" on re-establishing price stability
So, it should not have been a surprise that the policy rate would rise fast in 2022.
Instead, job gains were quite robust.
one might argue that it locked the Committee into holding the policy rate at the zero lower bound longer than was optimal.

parsed.rationale: The speaker explicitly backs another 75 bp hike in July and says the Fed is "all in" on restoring price stability, which is an explicit tightening signal. The retrospective argues that earlier guidance kept rates at zero too long and that rates need to rise fast toward neutral, which reinforces the hawkish lean.
